questions.subject: Biology
questions.q:
In an experiment, bacteria were grown for $500$ generations in a medium containing $^{14}\text{N}$ (light isotope), then transferred to a medium with $^{15}\text{N}$ (heavy isotope) for one generation, and finally transferred back to the $^{14}\text{N}$ medium for one more generation.

Assuming all cells divide synchronously and replication is semi-conservative, the ratio of $^{14}\text{N}^{15}\text{N}$ to $^{14}\text{N}^{14}\text{N}$ double-stranded DNA at the end of the experiment is:
questions.solution:
Initially, bacteria are grown in $^{14}\text{N}$ medium for $500$ generations, so all DNA molecules are $^{14}\text{N}^{14}\text{N}$ (light). Let the initial number of DNA molecules be $x$.

Upon transfer to $^{15}\text{N}$ medium for one generation, the DNA replicates semi-conservatively. The two $^{14}\text{N}$ strands of each molecule separate and act as templates to synthesize new $^{15}\text{N}$ strands. This results in $2x$ molecules of $^{14}\text{N}^{15}\text{N}$ (hybrid) DNA.

Upon transfer back to $^{14}\text{N}$ medium for one more generation, the $2x$ hybrid molecules separate into $2x$ strands of $^{14}\text{N}$ and $2x$ strands of $^{15}\text{N}$. Each strand synthesizes a new $^{14}\text{N}$ strand from the medium.

The $2x$ strands of $^{14}\text{N}$ form $2x$ molecules of $^{14}\text{N}^{14}\text{N}$ (light) DNA.

The $2x$ strands of $^{15}\text{N}$ form $2x$ molecules of $^{14}\text{N}^{15}\text{N}$ (hybrid) DNA.

The ratio of $^{14}\text{N}^{15}\text{N}$ to $^{14}\text{N}^{14}\text{N}$ double-stranded DNA at the end of the experiment is $2x : 2x = 1 : 1$.

Answer: $1:1$

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q:
DNA $\mathrm{C}_o \mathrm{t}$ analysis is based upon the principles of DNA renaturation kinetics. The rate at which heat-denatured DNA sequences in solution will renature is dependent on DNA concentration, re-association temperature, cation concentration, and viscosity (usually not a factor if the DNA is free of contaminants). Upon heat-denaturation of an entire genomic DNA, the rate at which a particular sequence will re-associate in a given buffer solution is proportional to the number of times the sequence is found in the genome. Given enough time, nearly all of the DNA in a heat-denatured sample will re-associate. Highly repetitive, moderately repetitive and non-repetitive are the three types of DNA sequences found normally in all genomes giving them different levels of complexity. Typical $\mathrm{C}_o$ t curves (see graph) were obtained for genomic DNA from three organisms ( $\mathbf{P}, \mathbf{Q}$ and $\mathbf{R}$ ).


Based on this information, select the correct option(s) from the following.
options: Genomic DNA of organism $\mathbf{P}$ is relatively less complex as compared to $\mathbf{Q}$ and $\mathbf{R}$.
Genomic DNA of organism $\mathbf{R}$ is relatively more complex that those of $\mathbf{P}$ and $\mathbf{Q}$.
Genomic DNA of organism $\mathbf{Q}$ is relatively more complex than that of $\mathbf{R}$.
Genomic DNA of organism $\mathbf{P}$ is relatively more complex than that of $\mathbf{R}$.

questions.q: Protein synthesis most often starts at AUG as a start codon and terminates at UAA, UAG and UGA as stop codons. Each codon specifies only one amino acid in all organisms. State which of the following statements is/are CORRECT.
options: The above information is consistent with the fact that the genetic code is universal.
Protein coding RNA from viruses, mammals or plants can be translated in bacteria.
In higher organisms, protein synthesis begins with methionine.
Use of more than one termination codon is more effective than a single termination codon in ensuring termination of protein synthesis.
